abstract: In the typical spatial search problems solved by continuous-time quantum walk, changing the location of the marked vertices does not alter the search problem. In this paper, we consider search when this is no longer true. In particular, we analytically solve search on the “simplex of $K_{M}$ complete graphs” with all configurations of two marked vertices, two configurations of $M+1$ marked vertices, and two configurations of $2(M+1)$ marked vertices, showing that the location of the marked vertices can dramatically influence the required jumping rate of the quantum walk, such that using the wrong configuration’s value can cause the search to fail. This sensitivity to the jumping rate is an issue unique to continuous-time quantum walks that does not affect discrete-time ones.

specification.problem: Continuous-time quantum walk spatial search on the simplex of K_M complete graphs, where the location of marked vertices changes the search problem; analyze configurations of two, M+1 and 2(M+1) marked vertices and how the optimal jumping rate depends on the configuration.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Assumed standard CTQW search setup and the qualitative dependence of the critical jumping rate on the marked-vertex configuration; the explicit analytic results are not in the abstract and are not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: jumping rate of the continuous-time quantum walk
number of complete graphs K_M in the simplex (and size of each)

equations.label: Search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Standard CTQW search Hamiltonian with oracle term over marked vertices. Its form is an assumption since the abstract does not state it.
equations.justification: Common convention for CTQW spatial search; not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Evolution
equations.description: Evolution from the uniform superposition initial state under H.
assumptions: Initial state is the uniform superposition |s>

registers.name: vertex
registers.size: N = number of vertices of the simplex of K_M (explicit count not given in abstract)
registers.role: Position register; computational basis states label graph vertices, evolved under H

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition |s> = N^{-1/2} sum_v |v> over all vertices.

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition |s> over all vertices.
Choose gamma (critical value depends on the marked-vertex configuration) and evolve under H for a time t.

specification.measurement: Measure the vertex register in the computational basis after evolution time t; success means obtaining a marked vertex (assumed).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Check whether the outcome is in the marked set; repeat if not. Using a gamma from the wrong configuration may make the search fail.
assumptions: Standard CTQW search Hamiltonian form and oracle strength 1 assumed; not stated in the abstract.
Vertex register of dimension N is an assumed encoding.
